headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure via shared file-based workflows; no direct data-leak or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman explicitly touches project notes, memory files, and CLAUDE.md and uses MCP, so it can ingest content that another agent may later treat as instructions. data-engineering-zoomcamp has no documented isolation or provenance controls, so a shared workspace or copied files would create a plausible injection path. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents read from the same workspace or copied files
IF either agent treats file contents as trusted instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable automatic instruction-following from shared files
Require provenance labels on imported notes
Review any CLAUDE.md or memory-file changes before reuse
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or trust-boundary enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show network_egress set to none, and neither profile documents shared filesystem access, OAuth, or secret handling. caveman touches session logs and memory files, but data-engineering-zoomcamp has no data-handling surface that would receive them by default. No plausible leakage path is evidenced from the pair.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem is introduced outside the profiles
IF either agent is reconfigured to upload file contents
mitigations: Keep both agents offline
Do not mount a shared workspace
Avoid placing secrets in project notes
Audit any future egress enablement
requires-engineering: add DLP controls if shared storage is later introduced

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and writes to files, while data-engineering-zoomcamp has no documented write surfaces or mutable-resource scopes. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely in the documented setup, but a shared directory or external orchestrator could still create collisions. The blast radius appears limited to local files.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF an external orchestrator gives data-engineering-zoomcamp write access not shown in the profile
mitigations: Use separate working directories
Serialize any file edits
Lock shared files during edits
Check for duplicate writes before saving
requires-engineering: add filesystem locking in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman can generate project notes and CLAUDE.md content that data-engineering-zoomcamp could reuse as course or workflow material, but the latter has no documented verification step or critical-action authority. Because the pairwise handoff is plausible through files and the downstream agent is not shown to critically evaluate inputs, the risk is a default workflow error rather than an irreversible action.
conditions: IF outputs from caveman are copied into data-engineering-zoomcamp inputs
IF data-engineering-zoomcamp uses those inputs without human review
mitigations: Require human review of transferred outputs
Mark generated notes as untrusted
Keep source and destination artifacts separate
Add a verification checklist before reuse
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware handoff

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented. Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, and neither shows regulated data handling or jurisdiction-specific constraints. With no compliance-relevant data class or policy gap evidenced, a breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data is later introduced into either agent
IF a jurisdiction-specific retention policy is imposed externally
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in both agents
Document any retention policy before use
Review future hosting jurisdiction
requires-engineering: add compliance controls if regulated data is introduced
